item.title: AI agent support matrix clarifies Defender for Endpoint’s activity-based discovery — 9 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 9 October 2026

AI agent support matrix clarifies Defender for Endpoint’s activity-based discovery

The period’s most consequential administrator guidance concerns local AI agents in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. A new support matrix covers supported agents, MCP server discovery, and runtime protection by operating system and configuration, while related pages clarify that discovery depends on observed activity. Sentinel also added specific custom-parser guidance. Most remaining updates—32 in Microsoft Security Exposure Management—were page-attribution maintenance.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

New matrix separates AI agent support by operating system and configuration

A new Microsoft Defender for Endpoint article documents supported local AI agents, MCP server discovery, and runtime protection scenarios, with support listed separately by operating system and configuration. It also explains that discovery depends on observed agent activity.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Installed agents may remain absent until Defender observes activity

The local-agent guidance states that Defender lists an agent after observing activity on an onboarded device; installation alone does not guarantee discovery. It also says the inventory is not a complete software inventory, directing administrators to Software inventory for installed-software details and the support matrix for coverage.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Runtime protection guidance broadens inspection-point terminology

The AI Agent Runtime Protection overview now uses broader descriptions of inspection points, streamlines its explanations of agent-native and network inspection, updates discovery terminology, and removes the explicit event-point list and vendor links.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel parser guidance sets disabled=false and conditions pack forwarding

Normalization guidance now explains that the generated table sets `disabled=false` to enable custom parsers and advises forwarding `pack` only when the source-specific parser supports it. Review custom unifying parser functions for these parameter expectations.

Exposure Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure

Exposure Management updates largely change page attribution

A broad Microsoft Security Exposure Management sweep changed author metadata across connector, attack-surface, and vulnerability/exposure pages. For example, the OT data connectors page now credits DebLanger instead of limwainstein/lwainstein. These edits indicate no administrator action.

item.title: Defender for Endpoint and Servers guidance details unified inventory, hunting, and RBAC — 8 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 8 October 2026

Defender for Endpoint and Servers guidance details unified inventory, hunting, and RBAC

This documentation-heavy period’s most consequential updates describe a combined Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers experience in the Microsoft Defender portal, clarify when disabling Defender for Servers automatically offboards eligible servers, and replace manual support-log analyzer steps with self-contained Live Response workflows. Sentinel normalization guidance also adds a unified process-event parser pattern, while most remaining edits are narrower reference, navigation, or release-entry maintenance.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Unified server experience guidance consolidates endpoint and server workflows

The Endpoint page now describes bringing Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers together in the Microsoft Defender portal for Azure and on-premises servers, covering server asset views, investigations, hunting, RBAC, and device groups. It states that existing Defender for Endpoint servers require no onboarding, reinstallation, or migration; administrators should still review capability requirements before changing configuration.

Defender for Cloud · Architecture and deployment

Offboarding guidance distinguishes disabling Defender for Servers from a Plan 2-to-Plan 1 switch

The Defender for Cloud tutorial states that disabling Defender for Servers for Azure subscriptions in public preview automatically offboards eligible servers, while switching from Plan 2 to Plan 1 does not trigger automatic offboarding. Administrators should account for that distinction when changing coverage.

Endpoint · Troubleshooting

Collect Support Log guidance moves to self-contained binary and Python actions

The updated Endpoint procedure replaces manual analyzer-download steps with self-contained binary or Python Live Response action pairs, adds package validation and workspace-ID handoff, and specifies prerequisites and HTTPS requirements. It also documents a local workflow for devices without Microsoft endpoint access; binary actions do not require Python, while Python actions do.

Sentinel · Developer and API

Sentinel normalization guidance adds the unified imProcessEvent parser

The normalization schema page now documents imProcessEvent for querying all process event types while retaining specialized parsers. It also revises custom-parser naming guidance and the filtering example, giving parser owners updated names and query patterns to apply.

Exposure Management · Developer and API

Azure DevOps connector setup now starts in Agentic code scanning management

The Exposure Management guide directs administrators to Agentic code scanning management, select Add another beside Source code environment, and choose Azure DevOps to open the connector flow. Connector configuration should follow that updated navigation.

View all updates for 8 October 2026 →

item.title: Defender for Identity details sensor v3.x activation without Defender for Endpoint — 6 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 6 October 2026

Defender for Identity details sensor v3.x activation without Defender for Endpoint

The period’s strongest operational changes affect Identity onboarding, Defender for Cloud KSPM scope, and Linux golden-image provisioning. Teams meeting-reporting setup and Sentinel’s ASIM Email Event reference also gained concrete guidance. Most remaining edits are navigation, capitalization, link, and wording maintenance.

Identity · Identity protection

Identity activation is limited to new sensor v3.x deployments

The updated guidance covers sensor v3.x activation without Defender for Endpoint on eligible Windows Server 2019 or later domain controllers. It applies only to new sensor v3.x deployments; automatic sensor activation and automatic Windows auditing require an active license that includes Microsoft Defender for Identity. Verify the operating system and licensing before using the method.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

KSPM recommendations move from running containers to workload controllers

Starting October 5, 2026, KSPM misconfiguration recommendations align with Kubernetes workload controllers rather than individual running container instances. Teams should look for findings against container deployment controllers when locating and triaging recommendations.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Linux golden-image guidance gates Defender startup on final hostnames

The deployment article now directs administrators to embed the tenant-specific onboarding file in the golden image, keep `mdatp` stopped during image creation, and start Defender on clones only after each final hostname is set. It also adds onboarding and health checks; image automation should protect the tenant-specific file and follow this startup sequence.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Teams meeting reporting now has an explicit Teams admin center control

The setup path now uses the Teams admin center’s `Allow users to report meetings` policy, while the Defender portal step remains to verify `Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams`. Use both controls when configuring meeting-report handling.

Sentinel · Developer and API

Sentinel adds a reference for normalized Email Event data

The new ASIM reference defines email routing, authentication, delivery-outcome, and threat fields, and documents the `_Im_EmailEvent` parser, custom parser naming, and filtering parameters. It provides a common basis for normalizing and querying email data across mail servers, gateways, and inspection systems.

item.title: Defender for Cloud Apps will auto-enable Identity inventory for eligible tenants October 15 — 5 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 5 October 2026

Defender for Cloud Apps will auto-enable Identity inventory for eligible tenants October 15

Starting October 15, 2026, the Defender for Cloud Apps integration with Identity inventory will move from opt-in to automatic enablement for eligible tenants without listed excluded configurations. Defender for Storage adds targeted on-demand scanning, while Defender for Cloud guidance adds integration prerequisites and Linux requirements. Microsoft also documents the Defender XDR Hunts experience for Defender Experts customers and clarifies Identity sensor v3 activation eligibility and operating mode.

Cloud Apps · Cloud and workloads

Identity inventory moves from opt-in to automatic enablement

The Defender for Cloud Apps release notes set October 15, 2026, as the date when Identity inventory integration will automatically enable for eligible tenants that do not use the listed excluded configurations.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Defender for Storage supports scoped malware scans

On-demand malware scanning can target individual blobs or files, containers or file shares, or objects matching a path prefix. REST API filters define the scope; without filters, the entire storage account is scanned.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Endpoint integration guidance adds prerequisite and sensor details

The Enable Defender For Endpoint guidance now states that the integration can use an existing Defender for Endpoint sensor from the same tenant. It also adds platform and Linux requirements plus checks for connectivity, proxy authentication, file-system settings, and security policies; Linux servers require Python 3.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

Hunts guidance defines access to expert-led investigations

The new Hunts overview describes how to view in-progress and completed expert-led hunts, including hunt types, statuses, outcomes, and supporting details in the Defender portal. The organization must be enrolled in Defender Experts Hunting, Plan 1, or Plan 2, and the user needs at least the Security Reader role in Microsoft Defender RBAC.

Identity · Identity protection

Identity sensor v3 activation eligibility is now explicit

The Activate Sensor guidance specifies support for new sensor v3.x deployments on eligible domain controllers without sensor v2.x. It also states that the standalone package activates sensor v3.x on Windows Sense in restricted identity-only mode.

View all updates for 5 October 2026 →

item.title: Custom detections spell out 5-minute-to-14-day scheduling and lookback boundaries — 4 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 4 October 2026

Custom detections spell out 5-minute-to-14-day scheduling and lookback boundaries

The period focuses on guidance changes that sharpen administrator decisions. Custom-detection pages spell out the 5-minute-to-14-day custom-frequency range, the Sentinel-only data-source boundary, fixed 4-hour-to-30-day lookbacks for Defender XDR data, and Sentinel lookback limits that remain in public preview. Other meaningful updates clarify Unified RBAC coverage for identity exclusions, restrict two Cloud Apps admin roles in new configurations, and record four GA Defender for Cloud sensor builds with security and dependency fixes.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

Custom frequency is restricted to Sentinel-only detections

Updated Custom Detection Rules guidance says custom frequency from 5 minutes to 14 days is available only for rules based exclusively on Microsoft Sentinel data. Rules using Defender XDR data instead use fixed lookback periods tied to run frequency, ranging from 4 hours to 30 days, and cannot use custom scoping with this frequency option.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel guidance sets preview lookback ceilings by frequency

The comparison guidance lists flexible and high-frequency support for Sentinel data: lookback is up to 48 hours when frequency exceeds one hour and up to 14 days when frequency is one hour or less. Lookback remains labeled public preview.

Defender XDR · General

Identity-exclusion guidance covers both response products

The updated guidance explains that identity exclusions affect automated response actions in both Defender for Identity and Defender for Endpoint. Its Unified RBAC permissions coverage now addresses both products’ data sources, role assignments, and data-source scope.

Cloud Apps · Cloud and workloads

Cloud Apps admin roles are unavailable for new configurations

App/instance admin and User group admin role assignments can no longer be used in new configurations. Existing configurations remain supported, and organizations needing these capabilities are directed to Microsoft Support.

Defender for Cloud · Identity protection

Defender for Cloud records four September GA sensor builds

The sensor changelog now lists versions 0.11.7, 0.10.10, 0.9.68, and 0.8.61 as September 2026 GA releases, each containing security vulnerability fixes and dependency updates.

View all updates for 4 October 2026 →

item.title: Defender for Office 365 rolls out promotional-mail tagging and automatic folder moves — 2 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 2 October 2026

Defender for Office 365 rolls out promotional-mail tagging and automatic folder moves

Defender for Office 365 will label promotional emails as “promotions” and can move them automatically to a Promotions folder, learning from user actions. Separately, the Office 365 permissions documentation removes the “related to Copilot” qualifier from descriptions of Data Security AI Admin DLP permissions while retaining the exclusion for prompt and response access.

Defender XDR · Email and collaboration

Promotional emails gain “promotions” labels and automatic folder handling

Microsoft says Defender for Office 365 will tag promotional emails as “promotions” and can automatically move them to a Promotions folder. The capability learns from user actions, and users can customize handling by moving messages. Public preview starts in mid-April 2026, with general rollout completing by late 2026.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Data Security AI Admin descriptions remove the Copilot qualifier

The Scc Permissions page now describes Data Security AI Admins and the Data Security AI Admin role as able to edit Data Loss Prevention policies without the previous “related to Copilot” qualifier. It continues to document access to view AI content, while prompt and response access remains excluded.

item.title: Central Linux scans and Teams reporting controls get sharper Defender administrator guidance — 1 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 1 October 2026

Central Linux scans and Teams reporting controls get sharper Defender administrator guidance

The substantive 1 October updates are mostly documentation guidance, but several now pin down settings and behaviors relevant to administrators. Endpoint guidance covers centrally scheduled Linux antivirus scans and clarifies secure-configuration scope; Defender for Office 365 provides more precise Teams reporting setup; Sentinel references add connector and table support details. Most of the remaining Defender for Business changes refresh navigation, terminology, and procedures.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Secure configuration guidance adds Windows Server 2022 and 2025

The updated Endpoint guidance now includes Windows Server 2022 and Windows Server 2025 in the device requirement. It also states that local administrator-defined antivirus exclusions are not honored by default and can be enabled through Defender or Intune policy.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Endpoint release guidance documents centrally scheduled Linux antivirus scans

The Microsoft Defender Endpoint Releases page now documents centrally scheduled Linux antivirus scans through managed JSON and Defender Portal policies. It also adds release information covering detection of critical Node.js, Python, and Java libraries, the libcurl 8.20.0 security update, and Windows Antivirus August 2026-2 fixes.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Teams reporting setup gains explicit portal and PowerShell destinations

The updated Teams submissions guidance points administrators to the Teams user reported settings page and provides Exchange Online PowerShell commands for viewing and configuring report destinations: Microsoft, a reporting mailbox, or both.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel connector references add Meraki File Scanned data and DCR support

The Cisco Meraki connector reference now documents File Scanned detections and the `CiscoMerakiFileScannedEvents_CL` table. It also marks the F5Telemetry LTM and RFI Playbook Alert Results tables as supported and documents workspace transform DCR support.

Business · Endpoint protection

Defender for Business clarifies which policy takes effect

The revised policy-order guidance states that only the highest-priority applicable policy is applied. Default policy priority remains fixed; newly created policies receive a priority, and moving them changes the position of default policies.

View all updates for 1 October 2026 →

item.title: Sentinel parser guidance forbids cross-table enrichment and preserves one output per source record — 8 September 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 8 September 2026

Sentinel parser guidance forbids cross-table enrichment and preserves one output per source record

The day’s most consequential updates sharpen Sentinel parser guidance and revise the documented severity of seven Azure Storage alerts to Informational. Defender XDR added dedicated guidance for mapping Advanced Hunting results into graphs, while Defender for Identity added resolution steps for the Sensor v3.x RPC Audit Misconfigured health alert. The remaining edits are primarily layout, link, terminology, and explanatory maintenance.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel parser guidance sets strict source and cardinality boundaries

The updated normalization guidance limits parsers to the declared source table, requires one normalized output per source record, and permits scalar or local static mappings. It explicitly prohibits cross-table enrichment, watchlists, multi-value expansion, joins, aggregation, and deduplication. Source filtering must use fields in the current event; missing source information should be handled in the connector or source-specific table.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel parser-creation guidance permits lookup mappings only with unique keys

The parser-creation skills guidance says each source record is normalized independently and record cardinality is preserved. Query-local datatable or lookup mappings are allowed when lookup keys are unique, while same-table and cross-table event enrichment are not used.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

New Defender XDR guidance details graph mapping for Advanced Hunting

The new guide explains how to prepare query results, configure graph nodes and edges, apply relationship conditions, and use recognized entity types and identifiers for Defender enrichment.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Azure Storage alert documentation now labels seven entries Informational

Seven documented Azure Storage alert entries now list their severity as Informational instead of High, Medium, or Low variants. Administrators reviewing the alert reference should use the revised labels when prioritizing those entries.

item.title: Sentinel table migration and Linux enforcement changes sharpen administrator action — 4 September 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 4 September 2026

Sentinel table migration and Linux enforcement changes sharpen administrator action

The period was dominated by documentation maintenance, but several updates carry direct operational weight. Sentinel guidance now points administrators from the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table to ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects, while Defender for Endpoint documents four Linux antivirus enforcement levels, a passive default, and Preview audit mode. Other consequential changes include SIEM-agent deprecation guidance for the Cloud Apps integration, manual Preview activation limits for Defender for Identity v3.x sensors on non-domain controllers, and material changes to the documented Defender XDR DataSecurityEvents schema.

Sentinel · Hunting and detection

Sentinel threat-intelligence content must move off the legacy table

The STIX guidance directs content to the ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects schemas and states that ingestion into the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table stops after July 31, 2025. Custom queries, analytics and detection rules, workbooks, and automation using the old table should be updated.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Linux antivirus enforcement now has four documented levels

The Linux configuration article lists four antivirus enforcement levels, identifies passive as the default, and marks audit mode as Preview. It adds verification guidance for the active level; audit mode requires Defender for Endpoint version 101.26062.0007 or later.

Cloud Apps · Cloud and workloads

Cloud Apps integration guidance now deprecates SIEM agents

The Sentinel integration page states that SIEM agents are deprecated while the Microsoft Sentinel integration (Preview) remains supported, and adds a dedicated integration section. Organizations still using SIEM agents should review their integration strategy against the supported Sentinel option.

Identity · Architecture and deployment

Defender for Identity documents manual v3.x activation on additional servers

The v3.x sensor deployment guidance now covers non-domain-controller AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers. Activation on those servers is in Preview and requires manual activation; automatic activation and migration are unsupported. Deployments limited to these servers should include at least one v3.x sensor on a domain controller.

Defender XDR · General

DataSecurityEvents reference adds and removes hunting columns

The Defender XDR table reference removes its Preview and prerelease notices, adds physical access, removable media, and risky AI usage fields, and removes several URL, email, file-path, workload, and Cloud App Alert fields. Query and integration owners should review dependencies on the removed columns.
